subject: Azure private offer — rebate reconciliation & channel split
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@retailcloud.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@retailcloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Reconciliation of rebate tiers + reseller passback for Azure PO

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the team found the latency guarantees compelling. Procurement is working through a draft private offer from Azure but we hit two sticking points we hoped Redwood could help clarify before we push to legal:

1) Rebate reconciliation: Azure wants to map rebates to list-price buckets but our finance team needs to confirm how those rebates net against committed consumption (true-up timing and lookback window). We need an explicit example that shows gross invoice -> rebate applied -> net revenue to Redwood.

2) Channel passback: our reseller (CloudBridge Partners) expects a clear statement of the reseller commission out of the private offer list price. They asked for a guaranteed minimum passback percentage for the first 12 months.

Can you provide a worked example (numbers) and confirm whether Redwood supports front-loaded vs annual true-up rebate options in the private offer? Also, please confirm any tax/treatment considerations that would impact the reseller share.

We'd like to finalize the PO by EOD Nov 10 if possible.

Best,
Sandeep
VP, Procurement
RetailCloud Inc.

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@retailcloud.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@retailcloud.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reconciliation of rebate tiers + reseller passback for Azure PO

Hi Sandeep — appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can support both front-loaded and true-up structures; we typically model both so finance can choose. Attached a short draft PO and a margin workback that walks through two example scenarios (front-load vs annual true-up) based on the list prices Azure will pass in the PO.

Highlights up front:
- We can show gross invoice -> rebate -> net revenue with sample numbers for a 12-month commitment.
- We recommend a reseller passback floor of 10–12% on net revenue for first 12 months (we included a 12% and 8% comparison in the workbook).
- Tax: reseller commission is computed net of VAT where applicable; for US deals most states won't change commission but we will confirm per-invoice tax treatment in the final doc.

I've looped in Ben (revenue ops) to confirm the margin math and Laura (channel ops) to confirm the recommended passback approach. Can you confirm the expected committed consumption and the reseller contact so we can tailor the example exactly?

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow (Nov 3) to walk the workbook then send updated PO v2 by Nov 6. Does that work?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Reconciliation of rebate tiers + reseller passback for Azure PO

Camila — quick notes from revenue ops side after skimming the workbook you attached:

- Worked example A (front-load): 12-month commitment $1.2M list -> Azure passes through private-offer list price. If we apply a 15% seller rebate at list, the gross invoice = $1,200,000; rebate = $180,000; Redwood net revenue before commission = $1,020,000.
  - Reseller passback at 12% (of Redwood net) = $122,400 -> Redwood net after passback = $897,600.
  - Recommended accounting: recognize Redwood net revenue monthly; record the reseller passback as a contra-revenue / commission expense.

- Worked example B (annual true-up): same list $1.2M but rebates accrue and true-up at year end. For cashflow, front-loading favors the reseller; for revenue recognition, true-up simplifies monthly deferral accounting but requires accruals.

- Tax note: if reseller invoices are grossed in certain states, we may need to gross-up commission. Need legal ops to confirm.

Attachments: I added a tab to channel_margin_workback.xlsx with the alternative 8%/12% splits and an illustrative month-by-month waterfall.

If RetailCloud wants a firm guaranteed minimum passback for 12 months, operations can support a contractual floor — recommend we structure it as a rebate-credit that flows with the PO and is subject to the Azure PO renewal cadence.

Ben
Revenue Operations Manager

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T14:37:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Reconciliation of rebate tiers + reseller passback for Azure PO

Adding channel ops perspective:

- Floor mechanics: we prefer a ‘‘floor then true-up" approach for commercial clarity — set a 12% guaranteed passback floor for months 1–12, then true-up vs actual usage at month 12. This protects the reseller while keeping ops manageable.
- We should include a short clause in the private offer that: (a) specifies passback percentage as % of Redwood net after vendor rebate, (b) defines tax treatment (commission is net of sales tax/V AT), and (c) defines the true-up lookback window (12 months).
- To avoid double-counting, ensure the PO's list price fields match the SKU mapping in our catalog — I flagged a couple of SKU mismatches in the draft PO (see Azure_PO_Draft_v2.pdf comments).

Suggested passback language (short): "Redwood will remit to the named reseller a passback equal to 12% of Redwood's net revenue from the committed private-offer list price for the first twelve (12) months; parties will reconcile actual usage and apply any true-up adjustments at the 12-month anniversary."

I'll also prep a version of the clause for US vs EU tax differences if needed.

Laura Bennett
Channel Operations Lead

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@retailcloud.com>, Maya Singh <maya.s@retailcloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T17:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Reconciliation of rebate tiers + reseller passback for Azure PO -- draft and next steps

Hi Sandeep / Maya —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are two artifacts: (1) Azure_PO_Draft_v2.pdf with SKU mapping notes from Laura, and (2) channel_margin_workback.xlsx with the front-load vs true-up examples. Summary of what we propose:

- Commercial model: we will show both the front-load and 12-month true-up worked examples. For contracting we recommend the "floor then true-up" route with a 12% passback floor for months 1–12, reconciled at the 12-month anniversary.
- Tax & accounting: reseller passback is computed on Redwood net after vendor rebate; commission will be treated as a contra-revenue / commission expense in our books. Where tax gross-up is required by law, we will annotate and partner with CloudBridge for apportionment.
- Operational asks for you: please confirm the committed consumption bands (estimated total list $) and the reseller legal entity name + billing contact for inclusion in the PO. If you can confirm by EOD Nov 10, we can issue the DocuSign PO for signature the week of Nov 13.

I've scheduled a 30-min walkthrough for Nov 9 at 11am PT — calendar invite sent. If that time doesn't work, let me know and we'll reschedule.

Thanks — attaching the files again here for convenience.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
